title: The Day of the Lord
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Day of the Lord is the decisive time of God’s judgment, vindication, deliverance, and final intervention. Scripture presents it as both warning to the wicked and hope for the people of God.
summary: The Day of the Lord is the decisive time of God’s judgment, vindication, deliverance, and final intervention. Scripture presents it as both warning to the wicked and hope for the people of God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ stands at the center of the final Day because He is the Lord who judges, delivers, and reigns. His return brings the Day of the Lord to its appointed fulfillment.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Day of the Lord is a major biblical theme of divine intervention. It includes judgment against evil, vindication of God’s name, deliverance for His people, and the coming fullness of His rule.

For the wicked, the Day is darkness, judgment, and terror. God will not ignore evil, idolatry, violence, pride, and rebellion forever.

For those who call on the Lord, the Day also brings hope. The same God who judges evil saves His people and brings righteousness to light.

The New Testament connects this Day with watchfulness, holiness, and the promised return of Christ. Believers are not children of darkness, but are called to live awake and sober.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
The Day of the Lord reminds people that history is accountable to God. Evil will not continue endlessly, and God’s patience should not be mistaken for indifference.

This doctrine should produce both repentance and hope. It warns the careless and strengthens those longing for God to make all things right.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as a child of the light. Do not mock God’s patience or become dull to His warnings. Call on the Lord, walk in holiness, and place your hope in Christ, who delivers His people and will judge the world in righteousness.
